Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. Wie ATTY. PETRONI F. FRADEJAS No. 001 Bonifacio cor. Magsaysay St. Barangay Liwayway, Odiongan Romblon Dear Atty. Fradejas: 105 s. 2010 This pertains to your letter seeking the Department's legal opinion on the following issues, to wit and we quote: 1) "What are the steps or procedure to be observed in enforcing or implementing the decision Of a Sangguniang Bayan in an administrative case filed against a Barangay Captain? Is there a need for this body to issue the corresponding writ of execution to enforce the decision? Is there a need for this body to pass a resolution or ordinance giving authority to the Municipal Mayor or anybody else to implement the decision? 2) What is the effect of the Order of Suspension issued by the Municipal Mayor against a Barangay Captain if there is no writ of execution cind/or Resolution from the Sangguniang Bayan to implement the decision? 3) What is the effect if the Municipal Mayor (without the writ of execution and a Resolution/Ordinance being issued) issues an order to the Police Officer to implement the decision? Could that order be considered as a valid or lawful order? Can a policeman be held liable for implementing that decision?" In reply to your first up to third queries, may we invite your attention to Sections 61, 62 and 66 of the Local Government Code, which provide, insofar as pertinent, that: "SEC. 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints.- A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows:

xxx -2- xxx xxx (c) A complaint against any elective barangay official shall be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory." "SEC. 62. Notice of Hearing.- (a) Within seven (7) days after the administrative complaint is filed, the Office Of the President or the sanggunian concerned, as the case may be, shall require the respondent to submit his verified answer within fifteen (15) days from receipt thereof, and commence the investigation of the case within ten (IO) days after receipt of the respondent." "SEC. 66. Form and Notice of Decision.- (a) The investigation of the case shall be terminated within ninety (90) days from the start thereof. Within thirty (30) days after the end of the investigation, the Office of the President or the Sanggunian concerned shall render a decision in writing stating clearly and distinctly the facts and the reasons for such decision." In view. of the above-cited provisions. it is clear that a verified complaint against any erring barangay elective official, in your case the Punong Barangay, shall be filed before the Sangguniang Bayan. Such being the case, after the Sangguniang Bayan concerned decided the administrative case within the time specified in the above-cited provision, the' Sanggunian concerned may direct the Local Chief Executive (Mayor) to implement its decision. In this regard, please be informed that if the Mayor is being directed by the Sanggunian to implement its decision or judgment rendered pursuant to the exercise of its quasi-judicial powers conferred by Section 61 of the Code, it is the ministerial duty of the Local Chief Executive to execute the same and he/she has no discretion to determine the propriety of the implementation of the decision or judgment.- The service or implementation of the decision/judgment has to be made without unnecessary delay so that after being duly informed, the respondent can immediately take steps to protect his interest by filing an appeal or apply for other appropriate relief. The refusal of the Local Chief Executive to implement the said decision can be considered as an obstruction of justice and, therefore, would tantamount to grave misconduct for which he/she may be administratively sanctioned. Please be informed further that the Sanggunian may direct the Local Chief Executive to implement the decision through a Resolution or by a mere Memorandum.

-3 With regard to the issuance of writ of execution by the Sanggunian concerned, please be informed that the Sanggunian has no power or authority to issue a writ of execution even in the exercise of its quasi-judicial function. Such power to issue a writ of execution is lodged only with the courts. Such being the case, the Local Chief Executive, who was directed to implement • a decision/judgment, shall implement the said decision/judgment even without the writ of execution issued by the court. Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. JESU . DO Director III Lega •94/La Director Rolando B. Calabazaron DILG Region IV-B Santos & Sons Bldg.. Aurora Blvd. Cubao, Quezon City
